S63.19.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with an active, enabled schedule
S63.19.note: The message after the click only reports that the run started; the finished result appears later in run history. The Run now icon also shows on paused schedules, where the click is refused with a message saying the schedule must be active and enabled.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud from the AGI Code sidebar.
Click More, then Work. In the Schedules part, hover an active schedule and click the play icon "Run now".
In the modal, click "Run it now".
Read the message that appears. Then click "Show recent runs" on the same schedule and check the newest run.
Compare with Expected: the run starts straight away and the run history shows it completing with a result.
S63.19.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Work > Schedules row, click the play icon tooltipped "Run now" (also in the Command Palette as "Code: Run Schedule Now")

S63.20.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one schedule
S63.20.note: The next-run text is shown in the Work list rows, not in a separate tree view; the Command Palette command "Code: Show Schedules" opens the same list.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud from the AGI Code sidebar.
Click More, then Work.
Read the description line on each schedule row.
Look for the next-run part: a future time reads "next in" followed by a duration, a past one reads "due" with "ago", and a paused or completed schedule reads "no next run".
Compare with Expected: each routine shows when it will next run.
S63.20.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Work > Schedules (each row's description line)

S63.21.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with a schedule that has run at least once, and ideally one whose last run failed
S63.21.note: "last run failed" appears only when the schedule carries a last error; the failure text itself is in the hover tooltip.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud from the AGI Code sidebar.
Click More, then Work.
Read the description line on each schedule row for the last-run part.
Look for "last ran" followed by a time, "never run", or "last run failed".
Compare with Expected: each routine shows when it last ran and whether that run failed.
S63.21.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Work > Schedules (each row's description line)

S63.22.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with a schedule that has past runs
S63.22.note: The list shows the newest 20 runs only.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud from the AGI Code sidebar.
Click More, then Work.
Hover a schedule row and click the history icon "Show recent runs".
If the schedule has never run, read the message saying it has not run yet. Otherwise read the list titled "Runs of" followed by the schedule name.
Compare with Expected: each past run shows its status and time, such as "Succeeded · <time>", newest first.
S63.22.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Work > Schedules row, click the history icon "Show recent runs" (also "Code: Show Schedule Runs" in the Command Palette)

labels.text: Pick a run to read its answer

S63.23.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with a schedule that has a run with output
S63.23.note: The extension keeps a run's answer in memory for the session; if it is no longer held, the tab says "This run's answer is no longer held here."
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud from the AGI Code sidebar.
Click More, then Work, then hover a schedule row and click "Show recent runs".
Pick a run that has an answer. The list placeholder reads "Pick a run to read its answer".
Read the text tab that opens. It has the schedule name as a heading, the run status line, and then the run's output text.
Compare with Expected: the run's output text is shown, not only its status. A run with no output opens nothing.
S63.23.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Work > Schedules row, click "Show recent runs", then pick a run in the list

S63.24.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with an active schedule
S63.24.note: A schedule that cannot be paused or resumed in its current state shows the message "this schedule cannot be paused or resumed in its current state." instead.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud from the AGI Code sidebar.
Click More, then Work. Hover an active schedule and click "Pause this schedule".
Read the progress message "pausing" and then check that the row description says "Paused".
Hover the same row and click "Resume this schedule".
Compare with Expected: the schedule pauses and resumes, and it stays in the list the whole time (nothing is deleted).
S63.24.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Work > Schedules row, click the icon "Pause this schedule" or "Resume this schedule" (also "Code: Pause Schedule" and "Code: Resume Schedule" in the Command Palette)

S63.32.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a schedule whose run has stopped to ask for a tool approval (produced by the server, not by a button in the app)
S63.32.note: The pause is decided on the server in apps/web (scheduled-agent-executor.ts and the tool-call gate), so the extension only shows and answers it; the extension does not show the resumed run itself, so the tester checks the run history.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud from the AGI Code sidebar and use a schedule whose run is waiting for approval (set up on the web).
Click More, then Work. Read the row description: it includes "a run is waiting for your approval".
Hover the schedule and click "Show recent runs". Pick the run whose status is "Waiting for approval".
In the modal that opens, read the request text and click "Approve".
Compare with Expected: the run resumes after approval. Check in "Show recent runs" that the run's status moves on from "Waiting for approval".
S63.32.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Work > Schedules row, click "Show recent runs", then pick the run labelled "Waiting for approval"

S63.33.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with a schedule that has missed or skipped a run (not something the app can create on demand)
S63.33.note: The explanation shows only when the run record holds missed-run details, which the extension reads and does not create; the reason appears in the run's detail text, not on the schedule row.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud from the AGI Code sidebar.
Click More, then Work. Hover a schedule that has a missed or skipped run and click "Show recent runs".
Find the run whose label starts with "Skipped" (or "Ran late" in its detail).

Read the detail text after the first dot separators. A missed run reads like "Skipped the run scheduled for <time>: it was missed by <duration>, and this schedule skips missed runs." A late run reads "Ran late: scheduled for <time>, started <duration> later."
Compare with Expected: the run history says that the occurrence was missed or skipped, and why.
S63.33.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Work > Schedules row, click "Show recent runs"
